The Buddha saw him and asked the monks why he was sitting there. The monks told him and the Buddha said, “Monks, should one eat anything that would stop one from hearing a teaching such as this?”

15.s: “No hetaṁ, bhante”.
15.e: “No, sir.”

15.s: “Na, bhikkhave, lasuṇaṁ khāditabbaṁ. Yo khādeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.
15.e: “You shouldn’t eat garlic. If you do, you commit an offense of wrong conduct.”

15.s: Tena kho pana samayena āyasmato sāriputtassa udaravātābādho hoti. Atha kho āyasmā mahāmoggallāno yenāyasmā sāriputto tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṁ sāriputtaṁ etadavoca— “pubbe te, āvuso sāriputta, udaravātābādho kena phāsu hotī”ti?
15.e: On one occasion Venerable Sāriputta had a stomachache. Venerable Mahāmoggallāna went to him and said, “When you had a stomachache in the past, Sāriputta, what made you better?”

15.s: “Lasuṇena me, āvuso”ti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
15.e: “Garlic.” They told the Buddha.

15.s: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ābādhappaccayā lasuṇaṁ khāditun”ti.
15.e: “I allow you to eat garlic if you’re sick.”

15.s: Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū ārāme tahaṁ tahaṁ passāvaṁ karonti. Ārāmo dussati. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
15.e: At that time there were monks who urinated here and there in the monastery. The monastery became filthy.

15.s: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ekamantaṁ passāvaṁ kātun”ti.
15.e: “You should urinate in one location.”

15.s: Ārāmo duggandho hoti …pe…
15.e: The monastery became smelly.

15.s: “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, passāvakumbhin”ti.
15.e: “I allow urine-collection pots.”

15.s: Dukkhaṁ nisinnā passāvaṁ karonti …pe…
15.e: It was painful to sit there while urinating.

15.s: “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, passāvapādukan”ti.
15.e: “I allow foot stands for urinating.”

15.s: Passāvapādukā pākaṭā honti. Bhikkhū hiriyanti passāvaṁ kātuṁ …pe…
15.e: The foot stands were unenclosed. The monks were embarrassed to urinate there.

15.s: “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, parikkhipituṁ tayo pākāre— iṭṭhakāpākāraṁ, silāpākāraṁ, dārupākāran”ti.
15.e: “I allow three kinds of encircling walls: walls of brick, stone, and wood.”

15.s: Passāvakumbhī apārutā duggandhā hoti …pe…
15.e: Not being covered, the urine-collection pots were smelly.

15.s: “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, apidhānan”ti.
15.e: “I allow lids.”

15.s: Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū ārāme tahaṁ tahaṁ vaccaṁ karonti. Ārāmo dussati. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
15.e: At that time there were monks who defecated here and there in the monastery. The monastery became filthy.

15.s: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ekamantaṁ vaccaṁ kātun”ti.
15.e: “You should defecate in one location.”

15.s: Ārāmo duggandho hoti …pe…
15.e: The monastery became smelly.

15.s: “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, vaccakūpan”ti.
15.e: “I allow cesspits.”

15.s: Vaccakūpassa kūlaṁ lujjati …pe…
15.e: The edge of the cesspit collapsed.

15.s: “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, cinituṁ tayo caye— iṭṭhakācayaṁ, silācayaṁ, dārucayan”ti.
15.e: “I allow you to construct three kinds of foundations: foundations of brick, stone, and wood.”

15.s: Vaccakūpo nīcavatthuko hoti, udakena otthariyyati …pe…
15.e: The cesspit was situated at a low point. It was flooded.

15.s: “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, uccavatthukaṁ kātun”ti.
15.e: “I allow you to raise the base.”

15.s: Cayo paripatati …pe…
15.e: The mound collapsed.

15.s: “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, cinituṁ tayo caye— iṭṭhakācayaṁ, silācayaṁ, dārucayan”ti.
15.e: “I allow you to construct three kinds of raised foundations: raised foundations of brick, stone, and wood.”

15.s: Ārohantā vihaññanti …pe…
15.e: It was difficult to get up to the cesspit.

15.s: “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, tayo sopāne— iṭṭhakāsopānaṁ, silāsopānaṁ, dārusopānan”ti.
15.e: “I allow three kinds of stairs: stairs of brick, stone, and wood.”

15.s: Ārohantā paripatanti …pe…
15.e: People fell down while climbing the stairs.

15.s: “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ālambanabāhan”ti.
15.e: “I allow rails.”

15.s: Ante nisinnā vaccaṁ karontā paripatanti …pe…
15.e: When seated on the edge to defecate, they fell down.

15.s: “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, santharitvā majjhe chiddaṁ katvā vaccaṁ kātun”ti.
15.e: “I allow you to lay a floor with a gap in the middle for defecating.”

15.s: Dukkhaṁ nisinnā vaccaṁ karonti …pe…
15.e: It was painful to sit there while defecating.

15.s: “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, vaccapādukan”ti.
15.e: “I allow foot stands for defecating.”

15.s: Bahiddhā passāvaṁ karonti …pe…
15.e: They urinated outside the cesspit.

15.s: “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, passāvadoṇikan”ti.
15.e: “I allow urinals.”

15.s: Avalekhanakaṭṭhaṁ na hoti …pe…
15.e: There were no wiping sticks.

15.s: “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, avalekhanakaṭṭhan”ti.
15.e: “I allow wiping sticks.”

15.s: Avalekhanapiṭharo na hoti …pe…
15.e: There was no container for the wiping sticks.

15.s: “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, avalekhanapiṭharan”ti.
15.e: “I allow containers for wiping sticks.”

15.s: Vaccakūpo apāruto duggandho hoti …pe…
15.e: Not being covered, the cesspit was smelly.

15.s: “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, apidhānan”ti.
15.e: “I allow lids.”

15.s: Ajjhokāse vaccaṁ karontā sītenapi uṇhenapi kilamanti …pe…
15.e: Because they were defecating outdoors, the monks were troubled by the cold and the heat.

15.s: “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, vaccakuṭin”ti.
15.e: “I allow restrooms.”

15.s: Vaccakuṭiyā kavāṭaṁ na hoti …pe…
15.e: The restrooms didn’t have doors.

15.s: “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, kavāṭaṁ piṭṭhasaṅghāṭaṁ udukkhalikaṁ uttarapāsakaṁ aggaḷavaṭṭiṁ kapisīsakaṁ sūcikaṁ ghaṭikaṁ tāḷacchiddaṁ āviñchanacchiddaṁ āviñchanarajjun”ti.
15.e: “I allow doors, door frames, lower hinges, upper hinges, door jambs, bolt sockets, bolts, latches, keyholes, door-pulling holes, and door-pulling ropes.”

15.s: Vaccakuṭiyā tiṇacuṇṇaṁ paripatati …pe…
15.e: Grass and dust fell into the restrooms.

15.s: “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ogumphetvā ullittāvalittaṁ kātuṁ— setavaṇṇaṁ kāḷavaṇṇaṁ gerukaparikammaṁ mālākammaṁ latākammaṁ makaradantakaṁ pañcapaṭikaṁ cīvaravaṁsaṁ cīvararajjun”ti.
15.e: “I allow you to firm up the structure and then to plaster it inside and outside, including: treating with white color, black color, and red ocher; making garland patterns, creeper patterns, shark-teeth patterns, and the fivefold pattern; putting up bamboo robe racks and clotheslines.”

15.s: Tena kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu jarādubbalo vaccaṁ katvā vuṭṭhahanto paripatati.
15.e: On one occasion a monk who was weak from old age fell over as he was getting up after defecating.

15.s: Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
“Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, olambakan”ti.
15.e: “I allow suspended ropes to hold onto.”

15.s: Vaccakuṭi aparikkhittā hoti …pe…
15.e: The restrooms were unenclosed.

15.s: “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, parikkhipituṁ tayo pākāre— iṭṭhakāpākāraṁ, silāpākāraṁ, dārupākāran”ti.
15.e: “I allow three kinds of encircling walls: walls of brick, stone, and wood.”

15.s: Koṭṭhako na hoti …pe…
15.e: There were no gatehouses.

15.s: “ anujānāmi, bhikkhave, koṭṭhakan”ti.
15.e: “I allow gatehouses.”

15.s: Koṭṭhakassa kavāṭaṁ na hoti …pe…
15.e: The gatehouses didn’t have doors.

15.s: “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, kavāṭaṁ piṭṭhasaṅghāṭaṁ udukkhalikaṁ uttarapāsakaṁ aggaḷavaṭṭiṁ kapisīsakaṁ sūcikaṁ ghaṭikaṁ tāḷacchiddaṁ āviñchanacchiddaṁ āviñchanarajjun”ti.
15.e: “I allow doors, door frames, lower hinges, upper hinges, door jambs, bolt sockets, bolts, latches, keyholes, door-pulling holes, and door-pulling ropes.”

15.s: Koṭṭhake tiṇacuṇṇaṁ paripatati …pe…
15.e: Grass and dust fell into the gatehouses.

15.s: “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ogumphetvā ullittāvalittaṁ kātuṁ— setavaṇṇaṁ kāḷavaṇṇaṁ gerukaparikammaṁ mālākammaṁ latākammaṁ makaradantakaṁ pañcapaṭikan”ti.
15.e: “I allow you to firm up the structure and then to plaster it inside and outside, including: treating with white color, black color, and red ocher; making garland patterns, creeper patterns, shark-teeth patterns, and the fivefold pattern.”

15.s: Pariveṇaṁ cikkhallaṁ hoti …pe…
15.e: The yards were muddy.

15.s: “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, marumbaṁ pakiritun”ti.
15.e: “I allow you to cover them with gravel.”

15.s: Na pariyāpuṇanti …pe…
15.e: They were unable to do it.

15.s: “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, padarasilaṁ nikkhipitun”ti.
15.e: “I allow you to lay paving stones.”

15.s: Udakaṁ santiṭṭhati …pe…
15.e: The water remained.

15.s: “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, udakaniddhamanan”ti.
15.e: “I allow water drains.”

15.s: Ācamanakumbhī na hoti …pe…
15.e: There were no restroom ablution pots.

15.s: “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ācamanakumbhin”ti.
15.e: “I allow restroom ablution pots.”

15.s: Ācamanasarāvako na hoti …pe…
15.e: There were no scoops for the ablution pots.

15.s: “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ācamanasarāvakan”ti.
15.e: “I allow scoops for the ablution pots.”

15.s: Dukkhaṁ nisinnā ācamenti …pe…
15.e: It was painful to sit there while washing.

15.s: “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ācamanapādukan”ti.
15.e: “I allow ablution foot stands.”

15.s: Ācamanapādukā pākaṭā honti, bhikkhū hiriyanti ācametuṁ …pe…
15.e: The foot stands were unenclosed. The monks were embarrassed to wash there.

15.s: “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, parikkhipituṁ tayo pākāre— iṭṭhakāpākāraṁ, silāpākāraṁ, dārupākāran”ti.
15.e: “I allow three kinds of encircling walls: walls of brick, stone, and wood.”

15.s: Ācamanakumbhī apārutā hoti, tiṇacuṇṇehipi paṁsukehipi okiriyyati …pe…
15.e: The restroom ablution pots were not covered. Grass, dust, and dirt fell into them.

15.s: “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, apidhānan”ti.
15.e: “I allow lids.”

15.s: Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū evarūpaṁ anācāraṁ ācaranti—
15.e: At one time the monks from the group of six were misbehaving in many ways.
15.t: Even more regulations on proper conduct and allowable requisites

15.s: mālāvacchaṁ ropentipi ropāpentipi, siñcantipi siñcāpentipi, ocinantipi ocināpentipi, ganthentipi ganthāpentipi, ekatovaṇṭikamālaṁ karontipi kārāpentipi, ubhatovaṇṭikamālaṁ karontipi kārāpentipi, mañjarikaṁ karontipi kārāpentipi, vidhūtikaṁ karontipi kārāpentipi, vaṭaṁsakaṁ karontipi kārāpentipi, āveḷaṁ karontipi kārāpentipi, uracchadaṁ karontipi kārāpentipi. Te kulitthīnaṁ kuladhītānaṁ kulakumārīnaṁ kulasuṇhānaṁ kuladāsīnaṁ ekatovaṇṭikamālaṁ harantipi harāpentipi, ubhatovaṇṭikamālaṁ harantipi harāpentipi, mañjarikaṁ harantipi harāpentipi, vidhūtikaṁ harantipi harāpentipi, vaṭaṁsakaṁ harantipi harāpentipi, āveḷaṁ harantipi harāpentipi, uracchadaṁ harantipi harāpentipi.
15.e: They planted flowering trees, watered and plucked them, and then tied the flowers together. They made the flowers into garlands, garlands with stalks on one side and garlands with stalks on both sides. They made flower arrangements, wreaths, ornaments for the head, ornaments for the ears, and ornaments for the chest. And they had others do the same. They then took these things, or sent them, to the women, the daughters, the girls, the daughters-in-law, and the female slaves of respectable families.

15.s: Te kulitthīhi kuladhītāhi kulakumārīhi kulasuṇhāhi kuladāsīhi saddhiṁ ekabhājanepi bhuñjanti, ekathālakepi pivanti, ekāsanepi nisīdanti, ekamañcepi tuvaṭṭenti, ekattharaṇāpi tuvaṭṭenti, ekapāvuraṇāpi tuvaṭṭenti, ekattharaṇapāvuraṇāpi tuvaṭṭenti, vikālepi bhuñjanti, majjampi pivanti, mālāgandhavilepanampi dhārenti, naccantipi, gāyantipi, vādentipi, lāsentipi; naccantiyāpi naccanti, naccantiyāpi gāyanti, naccantiyāpi vādenti, naccantiyāpi lāsenti …pe… lāsentiyāpi naccanti, lāsentiyāpi gāyanti, lāsentiyāpi vādenti, lāsentiyāpi lāsenti;
15.e: They ate from the same plates as these women and drank from the same vessels. They sat on the same seats as them, and they lay down on the same beds, on the same sheets, under the same covers, and both on the same sheets and under the same covers. They ate at the wrong time, drank alcohol, and wore garlands, perfumes, and cosmetics. They danced, sang, played instruments, and performed. While the women were dancing, singing, playing instruments, and performing, so would they.

15.s: aṭṭhapadepi kīḷanti, dasapadepi kīḷanti, ākāsepi kīḷanti, parihārapathepi kīḷanti, santikāyapi kīḷanti, khalikāyapi kīḷanti, ghaṭikāyapi kīḷanti, salākahatthenapi kīḷanti, akkhenapi kīḷanti, paṅgacīrenapi kīḷanti, vaṅkakenapi kīḷanti, mokkhacikāyapi kīḷanti, ciṅgulakenapi kīḷanti, pattāḷhakenapi kīḷanti, rathakenapi kīḷanti, dhanukenapi kīḷanti, akkharikāyapi kīḷanti, manesikāyapi kīḷanti, yathāvajjenapi kīḷanti;
15.e: They played various games: eight-row checkers, ten-row checkers, imaginary checkers, hopscotch, pick-up-sticks, board games, tipcat, painting with the hand, dice, leaf flutes, toy plows, somersaults, pinwheels, toy measures, toy carriages, toy bows, guessing from syllables, thought guessing, mimicking deformities.

15.s: hatthismimpi sikkhanti, assasmimpi sikkhanti, rathasmimpi sikkhanti, dhanusmimpi sikkhanti; tharusmimpi sikkhanti; hatthissapi purato dhāvanti, assassapi purato dhāvanti, rathassapi purato dhāvantipi ādhāvantipi; usseḷentipi, apphoṭentipi, nibbujjhantipi, muṭṭhīhipi yujjhanti; raṅgamajjhepi saṅghāṭiṁ pattharitvā naccakiṁ evaṁ vadanti— “idha, bhagini, naccassū”ti; nalāṭikampi denti; vividhampi anācāraṁ ācaranti.
15.e: They trained in elephant riding, in horsemanship, in carriage riding, in archery, in swordsmanship. And they ran in front of elephants, horses, and carriages, and they ran backward and forward. They whistled, clapped their hands, wrestled, and boxed. They spread their outer robe on a stage and said to the dancing girls, “Dance here, sister,” and they made gestures of approval. And they misbehaved in a variety of ways.

15.s: Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ …pe…
15.e: They told the Buddha. Soon afterwards he gave a teaching and addressed the monks:

15.s: “na, bhikkhave, vividhaṁ anācāraṁ ācaritabbaṁ. Yo ācareyya, yathādhammo kāretabbo”ti.
15.e: “You shouldn’t engage in various kinds of misbehavior. If you do, you should be dealt with according to the rule.”

15.s: Tena kho pana samayena āyasmante uruvelakassape pabbajite saṅghassa bahuṁ lohabhaṇḍaṁ dārubhaṇḍaṁ mattikābhaṇḍaṁ uppannaṁ hoti. Atha kho bhikkhūnaṁ etadahosi— “kiṁ nu kho bhagavatā lohabhaṇḍaṁ anuññātaṁ, kiṁ ananuññātaṁ; kiṁ dārubhaṇḍaṁ anuññātaṁ, kiṁ ananuññātaṁ; kiṁ mattikābhaṇḍaṁ anuññātaṁ, kiṁ ananuññātan”ti? Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṁ nidāne etasmiṁ pakaraṇe dhammiṁ kathaṁ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi—
15.e: At the time of Venerable Uruvelakassapa’s going forth, the Sangha was offered a large number of iron, wooden, and ceramic goods. The monks thought, “Which iron, wooden, and ceramic goods have been allowed by the Buddha, and which not?” They told the Buddha. The Buddha then gave a teaching and addressed the monks:

15.s: “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ṭhapetvā paharaṇiṁ sabbaṁ lohabhaṇḍaṁ, ṭhapetvā āsandiṁ pallaṅkaṁ dārupattaṁ dārupādukaṁ sabbaṁ dārubhaṇḍaṁ, ṭhapetvā katakañca kumbhakārikañca sabbaṁ mattikābhaṇḍan”ti.
15.e: “I allow all iron goods except weapons; all wooden goods except high couches, luxurious couches, wooden almsbowls, and wooden shoes; and all ceramic goods except ceramic foot scrubbers and clay huts.”

15.s:
Vallikāpi ca pāmaṅgo,
kaṇṭhasuttaṁ na dhāraye;
Kaṭi ovaṭṭi kāyuraṁ,
hatthābharaṇamuddikā.
15.e:
And earrings, hanging strings,
shouldn’t wear a necklace;
Hips, bangles, armlets,
Bracelets, rings.

15.s:
Dīghe kocche phaṇe hatthe,
sitthā udakatelake;
Ādāsudapattavaṇā,
ālepommaddacuṇṇanā.
15.e:
Long, brush, comb, hands,
Beeswax, water and oil;
Sores in a mirror or bowl of water,
Ointment, creams, powder.

15.s:
Lañchenti aṅgarāgañca,
mukharāgaṁ tadūbhayaṁ;
Cakkhurogaṁ giraggañca,
āyataṁ sarabāhiraṁ.
15.e:
They applied, and body cosmetics,
Facial cosmetics, both;
Eye disease, and hilltop,
drawn-out voice, outside.

15.s:
Ambapesisakalehi,
ahicchindi ca candanaṁ;
Uccāvacā pattamūlā,
suvaṇṇo bahalā valī.
15.e:
Mangoes, pieces, with whole,
Snake, and cut off, sandal;
Luxurious, bowl bottoms,
Gold, thick, marks.

15.s:
Citrā dussati duggandho,
uṇhe bhijjiṁsu miḍḍhiyā;
Paribhaṇḍaṁ tiṇaṁ coḷaṁ,
mālaṁ kuṇḍolikāya ca.
15.e:
Colorful, stained, smelly,
In the heat, they broke, on a bench;
Ledge, straw, cloth,
Platform, and container.

15.s:
Thavikā aṁsabaddhañca,
tathā bandhanasuttakā;
Khile mañce ca pīṭhe ca,
aṅke chatte paṇāmanā.
15.e:
Bag, and shoulder strap,
So a string for fastening;
From a peg, and on a bed, and on a bench,
In the lap, on a sunshade, opening.

15.s:
Tumbaghaṭichavasīsaṁ,
calakāni paṭiggaho;
Vipphālidaṇḍasovaṇṇaṁ,
patte pesi ca nāḷikā.
15.e:
Gourd, waterpots, skull,
Chewed food remnants, trash can;
Tore, handle, gold,
Feather, and piece, cylinder.

15.s:
Kiṇṇasattu saritañca,
madhusitthaṁ sipāṭikaṁ;
Vikaṇṇaṁ bandhivisamaṁ,
chamājirapahoti ca.
15.e:
Yeast, flour, and stone powder,
Beeswax, case;
Deformed corners, tied down, uneven,
Ground, deteriorating, and not right.

15.s:
Kaḷimbhaṁ moghasuttañca,
adhotallaṁ upāhanā;
Aṅgule paṭiggahañca,
vitthakaṁ thavikabaddhakā.
15.e:
Ruler, and guide line,
Dirty, wet, sandals;
Finger, and thimble,
Small bowl, bag, strap.

15.s:
Ajjhokāse nīcavatthu,
cayo cāpi vihaññare;
Paripati tiṇacuṇṇaṁ,
ullittaavalittakaṁ.
15.e:
Outside, low base,
And also the mound, they had difficulty;
Fell down, grass and dust,
Plaster inside and outside.

15.s:
Setaṁ kāḷakavaṇṇañca,
parikammañca gerukaṁ;
Mālākammaṁ latākammaṁ,
makaradantakapāṭikaṁ.
15.e:
White, and black color,
And treating with red ocher;
Making a garland pattern, and a creeper pattern,
A shark-teeth pattern, pattern.

15.s:
Cīvaravaṁsaṁ rajjuñca,
anuññāsi vināyako;
Ujjhitvā pakkamanti ca,
kathinaṁ paribhijjati.
15.e:
Bamboo robe rack, and line,
Did the Leader allow;
Abandoned and left,
The frame broke.

15.s:
Viniveṭhiyati kuṭṭepi,
pattenādāya gacchare;
Thavikā bandhasuttañca,
bandhitvā ca upāhanā.
15.e:
Unfolded, and against a wall,
Taking their bowls they went;
Bag, and fastening string,
And bound the sandals.

15.s:
Upāhanatthavikañca,
aṁsabaddhañca suttakaṁ;
Udakākappiyaṁ magge,
parissāvanacoḷakaṁ.
15.e:
And sandal bag,
And shoulder strap, string;
Unallowable water while traveling,
Water filter, cloth.

15.s:
Dhammakaraṇaṁ dve bhikkhū,
vesāliṁ agamā muni;
Daṇḍaṁ ottharakaṁ tattha,
anuññāsi parissāvanaṁ.
15.e:
Water strainer, two monks,
The Sage went to Vesālī;
Wooden frame, spreading there,
He allowed a filter.

15.s:
Makasehi paṇītena,
bahvābādhā ca jīvako;
Caṅkamanajantāgharaṁ,
visame nīcavatthuko.
15.e:
With mosquitoes, with fine,
And often sick, Jīvaka;
Walking-meditation paths, sauna,
On uneven, low base.

15.s:
Tayo caye vihaññanti,
sopānālambavedikaṁ;
Ajjhokāse tiṇacuṇṇaṁ,
ullittaavalittakaṁ.
15.e:
Three foundations, they had difficulty,
Stairs, rails, railings;
Outside, grass and dust,
Plastered inside and outside.

15.s:
Setakaṁ kāḷavaṇṇañca,
parikammañca gerukaṁ;
Mālākammaṁ latākammaṁ,
makaradantakapāṭikaṁ.
15.e:
White, and black color,
And treating with red ocher;
Making a garland pattern, and a creeper pattern,
A shark-teeth pattern, pattern.

15.s:
Vaṁsaṁ cīvararajjuñca,
uccañca vatthukaṁ kare;
Cayo sopānabāhañca,
kavāṭaṁ piṭṭhasaṅghāṭaṁ.
15.e:
Bamboo, and clothesline,
And should raise the base;
Mound, and stairs, rails,
Door, door frame.

15.s:
Udukkhaluttarapāsakaṁ,
vaṭṭiñca kapisīsakaṁ;
Sūcighaṭitāḷacchiddaṁ,
āviñchanañca rajjukaṁ.
15.e:
Lower hinge, upper hinge,
Door jamb, bolt socket;
Bolt, latch, keyhole,
And door-pulling, rope.

15.s:
Maṇḍalaṁ dhūmanettañca,
majjhe ca mukhamattikā;
Doṇi duggandhā dahati,
udakaṭṭhānaṁ sarāvakaṁ.
15.e:
Encircling trench, and flue,
And in the middle, clay for the face;
Trough, smelly, scorched,
Water place, scoop.

15.s:
Na sedeti ca cikkhallaṁ,
dhovi niddhamanaṁ kare;
Pīṭhañca koṭṭhake kammaṁ,
marumbā silā niddhamanaṁ.
15.e:
And did not sweat, muddy,
Wash, should make a drain;
And bench, gatehouse, making,
Gravel, stones, drain.

15.s:
Naggā chamāya vassante,
paṭicchādī tayo tahiṁ;
Udapānaṁ lujjati nīcaṁ,
valliyā kāyabandhane.
15.e:
Naked, on the ground, raining,
Three coverings there;
Well, collapsed, low,
With creepers, belt.

15.s:
Tulaṁ kaṭakaṭaṁ cakkaṁ,
bahū bhijjanti bhājanā;
Lohadārucammakhaṇḍaṁ,
sālātiṇāpidhāni ca.
15.e:
Well-sweep, pulley, wheel,
Many vessels broke;
Iron, wood, hide,
House, grass, and cover.

15.s:
Doṇicandani pākāraṁ,
cikkhallaṁ niddhamanena ca;
Sītigataṁ pokkharaṇiṁ,
purāṇañca nillekhaṇaṁ.
15.e:
Trough, disposal area, wall,
Muddy, and with a drain;
Cold, lotus bathing tank,
And stagnant, pointed roof.

15.s:
Cātumāsaṁ sayanti ca,
namatakañca nadhiṭṭhahe;
Āsittakaṁ maḷorikaṁ,
bhuñjantekaṁ tuvaṭṭeyyuṁ.
15.e:
Four months, and they slept,
And piece of felt, should not determine;
Heating, stand,
They ate from one, they lay down.

15.s:
Vaḍḍho bodhi na akkami,
ghaṭaṁ katakasammajjani;
Sakkharaṁ kathalañceva,
pheṇakaṁ pādaghaṁsanī.
15.e:
Vaḍḍha, Bodhi, he did not step on,
Waterpot, ceramic foot scrubber, broom;
Stone, and pebbles,
Pumice foot scrubbers.

15.s:
Vidhūpanaṁ tālavaṇṭaṁ,
makasañcāpi cāmarī;
Chattaṁ vinā ca ārāme,
tayo sikkāya sammuti.
15.e:
Standard fan, palm-leaf fan,
And mosquito, yak-tail;
Sunshade, and without, in a monastery,
Three with agreement on carrying net.

15.s:
Romasitthā nakhā dīghā,
chindantaṅgulikā dukkhā;
Salohitaṁ pamāṇañca,
vīsati dīghakesatā.
15.e:
Regurgitator, rice, long nails,
Cutting, the fingers hurt;
Bled, and even,
Twenty, long haired.

15.s:
Khuraṁ silaṁ sipāṭikaṁ,
namatakaṁ khurabhaṇḍakaṁ;
Massuṁ kappenti vaḍḍhenti,
golomicaturassakaṁ.
15.e:
Razor, stone, case,
Felt, barber equipment;
They trimmed beards, grew them long,
Goatee, sideburns.

15.s:
Parimukhaṁ aḍḍhadukañca,
dāṭhisambādhasaṁhare;
Ābādhā kattarivaṇo,
dīghaṁ sakkharikāya ca.
15.e:
Circle beard, and chest hair,
Mustache, would remove from private parts;
Disease, sore with scissors,
Long, and small stones.

15.s:
Palitaṁ thakitaṁ uccā,
lohabhaṇḍañjanī saha;
Pallatthikañca āyogo,
vaṭaṁ salākabandhanaṁ.
15.e:
Gray, blocked, luxurious,
Metal goods, with ointment box;
And clasping the knees, back-and-knee strap,
Weft, shuttle, belt.

Multiple string belt, water snake head belt,
Belts of twisted strings of various colors,
belts like ornamental ropes;
Strips of cloth, and pigs’ intestines,
Edges, twisted strings of various colors, ornamental ropes;
End, loop, and knot,
Also the loop at the end wore away.

15.s:
Gaṇṭhikā uccāvacañca,
phalakantepi ogāhe;
Gihivatthaṁ hatthisoṇḍaṁ,
macchakaṁ catukaṇṇakaṁ.
15.e:
Toggles, and luxurious,
Also should insert a shield at the edge;
Sarongs like householders, elephant trunk,
Fish style, four-corner style.

15.s:
Tālavaṇṭaṁ satavali,
gihipārutapārupaṁ;
Saṁvelli ubhatokājaṁ,
dantakaṭṭhaṁ ākoṭane.
15.e:
Palm leaf, hundred fold,
Wearing upper robes like householders;
Loin cloths, carrying poles with loads on both ends,
Tooth cleaner, smacking.

15.s:
Kaṇṭhe vilaggaṁ dāyañca,
paṭaggi rukkhahatthinā;
Yameḷe lokāyatakaṁ,
pariyāpuṇiṁsu vācayuṁ.
15.e:
Stuck in the throat, and forest,
Counterfire, tree, with elephant;
Yameḷa, cosmological theory,
They learned, they taught.

15.s:
Tiracchānakathā vijjā,
khipi maṅgalaṁ khādi ca;
Vātābādho dussati ca,
duggandho dukkhapādukā.
15.e:
Worldly talk, knowledge,
He sneezed, blessing, and he ate;
Stomachache, and became filthy,
Smelly, painful, foot stands.

15.s:
Hiriyanti pāruduggandho,
tahaṁ tahaṁ karonti ca;
Duggandho kūpaṁ lujjanti,
uccavatthu cayena ca.
15.e:
They were embarrassed, covered, smelly,
And they did it here and there;
Smelly, cesspit, collapsed,
Raised base, and with foundation.

15.s:
Sopānālambanabāhā,
ante dukkhañca pādukā;
Bahiddhā doṇi kaṭṭhañca,
piṭharo ca apāruto.
15.e:
Stairs, rails,
On the edge, and painful, foot stands;
Outside, urinal, and sticks,
And container, uncovered.

15.s:
Vaccakuṭiṁ kavāṭañca,
piṭṭhasaṅghāṭameva ca;
Udukkhaluttarapāso,
vaṭṭiñca kapisīsakaṁ.
15.e:
Restroom, and door,
And just the door frame;
Lower hinge, upper hinge,
And door jamb, bolt socket.

15.s:
Sūcighaṭitāḷacchiddaṁ,
āviñchanacchiddameva ca;
Rajju ullittāvalittaṁ,
setavaṇṇañca kāḷakaṁ.
15.e:
Bolt, latch, keyhole,
And just a door-pulling hole;
Rope, plastered inside and outside,
And white color, black.

15.s:
Mālākammaṁ latākammaṁ,
makaraṁ pañcapaṭikaṁ;
Cīvaravaṁsaṁ rajjuñca,
jarādubbalapākāraṁ.
15.e:
Making a garland pattern, a creeper pattern,
Shark, the fivefold pattern;
Bamboo robe rack, and line,
Weak from old age, wall.

15.s:
Koṭṭhake cāpi tatheva,
marumbaṁ padarasilā;
Santiṭṭhati niddhamanaṁ,
kumbhiñcāpi sarāvakaṁ.
15.e:
And so also just a gatehouse,
Gravel, paving stones;
Remained, drain,
And also pot, scoop.

15.s:
Dukkhaṁ hiri apidhānaṁ,
anācārañca ācaruṁ;
Lohabhaṇḍaṁ anuññāsi,
ṭhapayitvā paharaṇiṁ.
15.e:
Painful, embarrassed, lid,
And they misbehaved;
He allowed iron goods,
Except weapons.

15.s:
Ṭhapayitvāsandipallaṅkaṁ,
dārupattañca pādukaṁ;
Sabbaṁ dārumayaṁ bhaṇḍaṁ,
anuññāsi mahāmuni.
15.e:
Except high couches and luxurious couches,
And wooden almsbowls, wooden shoes;
All wooden goods,
The Great Sage allowed.

15.s:
Katakaṁ kumbhakārañca,
ṭhapayitvā tathāgato;
Sabbampi mattikābhaṇḍaṁ,
anuññāsi anukampako.
15.e:
Ceramic foot scrubbers, and clay huts,
The Buddha having excepted;
Also all clay goods,
The Compassionate One allowed.

15.s:
Yassa vatthussa niddeso,
purimena yadi samaṁ;
Tampi saṅkhittaṁ uddāne,
nayato taṁ vijāniyā.
15.e:
The details of the topics,
If the same as the preceding,
Is also found in brief in the summary verses,
For the purpose of guiding those who have understood it.

15.s:
Evaṁ dasasatā vatthū,
vinaye khuddakavatthuke;
Saddhammaṭṭhitiko ceva,
pesalānañcanuggaho.
15.e:
Thus there are one hundred and ten topics
In the chapter on minor topics in the Monastic Law.
Indeed, the true Teaching will be long lived,
And good people will be supported.

15.s:
Susikkhito vinayadharo,
hitacitto supesalo;
Padīpakaraṇo dhīro,
pūjāraho bahussutoti.
15.e:
A well-trained expert in the Monastic Law,
A good person intent on what’s beneficial,
A wise one, lighting a lamp—
This is a learned one worthy of homage.”
